threats.title: Merchant API Key Spoofing via Non-Constant-Time HMAC Verification
threats.attackerPrecondition: Network adversary with the ability to measure API response timing differences
threats.attackNarrative: An attacker sends forged HMAC merchant signatures to the Core Payment API. Because string comparison terminates early on mismatched bytes, the attacker measures latency differences over repeated requests to reconstruct valid authentication tokens character-by-character, impersonating legitimate merchants.
threats.impactRationale: Compromise of merchant authentication allows unauthorized transaction settlements.
threats.likelihoodRationale: Requires low-jitter network measurements and high request volumes across rate limiters.
recommendedMitigations: Use crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare in Go Gin handler
Enforce replay nonce and reject timestamp skews greater than 300 seconds

threats.title: Payment Token Tampering via Unsigned Webhook Payload Injection
threats.attackerPrecondition: Adversary positioned to intercept or proxy webhook traffic
threats.attackNarrative: An attacker tampers with transaction amount parameters in transit between the merchant client and the payment gateway edge. Without cryptographic integrity checks on the payload, the backend records the lower modified amount while clearing the original goods.
threats.impactRationale: Financial loss through price manipulation and fraudulent transaction settlement.
threats.likelihoodRationale: Mitigated by mandatory TLS transport unless client trust store is compromised.
recommendedMitigations: Digitally sign webhook payloads using ECDSA or HMAC with symmetric secret
Verify merchant signature headers prior to processing payload bodies
